newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten turns to Confucius in final HK days.
newsitem.headline: Patten turns to Confucius in final HK days.

text.p: British Governor Chris Patten turned to ancient Chinese philopher Confucius on Friday to explain why he was leaving the British colony with his head held high as a gentleman.
Patten, who spent five years battling China over Hong Kong's return to Beijing, also revealed he did not set store in the Chinese idea of "face", the concept of maintaining pride.

Answering questions in a phone-in radio programme ahead of his departure next Monday evening at the end of Britain's 156-year colonial rule, Patten said all politicans learned to live with setbacks to their pride.
"If you are democratic, if you are an elected politician, face is not the most important thing you have to be concerned about," Patten said.
"I think what is much more important is dignity and honour and honesty," he added.
Quoting from the Analects of Confucius, Patten said the philosopher told a student who asked for a definition of a gentleman:
"Well, a gentleman, he is sent by his lord to serve in the four quarters of the globe and if he doesn't bring disgrace on his lord, that is a gentleman".
"And I think that matters much more to me than face," Patten added.
